findings.evidenceJa: セイバー本人が頑なに拒む
findings.governingReading: Shirou expects Saber herself to refuse stubbornly.
findings.explanation: Surely preserves confidence but omits the obstinate firmness that defines Saber’s agency here.

findings.evidenceJa: 浮かない顔
findings.governingReading: Illya notices Shirou looking glum or downcast.
findings.explanation: Serious replaces visible dejection with a broader neutral expression.

findings.highlight: It’s going to get cold today
findings.evidenceJa: 今日は冷える
findings.governingReading: Shirou says that today is cold and tells Illya to go home.
findings.explanation: Going to get cold shifts the existing cold into a future forecast.

findings.evidenceJa: セイバーが消えかけてる
findings.governingReading: Illya states that Saber is already in the process of disappearing.
findings.explanation: Going to disappear removes the ongoing deterioration that Illya claims to know about.

findings.evidenceJa: なんで、そんな事、を
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks why Illya would say or do such a thing as her hostility and paralysis emerge.
findings.explanation: The English invents an epistemic question about how she learned the Rider incident, redirecting his alarm away from her conduct.

findings.evidenceJa: 視界が途切れた
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s field of vision cuts out abruptly.
findings.explanation: Fades makes the loss gradual and softens the severing motif repeated when consciousness cuts out.

findings.evidenceJa: ようやく、意識もブツリと途切れてくれた
findings.governingReading: At last, while he cannot tell whether he lives or has died, Shirou’s consciousness mercifully snaps off as well.
findings.explanation: Fades away omits the abrupt snapping sound and the relief carried by ようやく and くれた.

findings.evidenceJa: 簡単に殺させる
findings.governingReading: The recollected line says that, without means to fight, Shirou can easily be made or allowed to be killed.
findings.explanation: The English repeats the earlier direct threat and erases the causative distinction explicitly present in this recollection.

findings.evidenceJa: まともに戦えない
findings.governingReading: Without Saber, Shirou cannot fight properly or on equal terms.
findings.explanation: At all turns severe inadequacy into total incapacity, conflicting with the limited actions he has already taken.

findings.evidenceJa: 滅多刺しだった
findings.governingReading: Rider stabbed and slashed Shirou repeatedly.
findings.explanation: Beating replaces the weapon injuries with blunt assault and breaks the connection to his body being cut all over.

findings.evidenceJa: 目の前の惨事
findings.governingReading: Shirou could not stop the catastrophe unfolding before his eyes.
findings.explanation: Around me disperses a directly witnessed scene into a general surrounding disaster.

findings.evidenceJa: 正義の味方
findings.governingReading: Shirou thinks of the ally of justice he has admired since childhood.
findings.explanation: Superhero substitutes a different cultural archetype and weakens the fixed phrase governing Shirou’s inherited ideal.

findings.evidenceJa: 全身が震えている
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s whole body trembles under the conviction that he must win.
findings.explanation: Demanding personifies the body as issuing the imperative rather than physically manifesting his desperation.

findings.evidenceJa: 格闘には向かない
findings.governingReading: Archer’s remembered judgment is that Emiya Shirou is unsuited to martial or close combat.
findings.explanation: Fighting broadens the limitation to every kind of battle and blurs the following contrast with a mental struggle.

findings.highlight: I realize that more than ever now
findings.evidenceJa: 嫌というほど思い知らされた
findings.governingReading: Shirou has been made to learn the fact to a sickening or painful degree.
findings.explanation: More than ever preserves increased conviction but removes the punishing force of the lesson.

findings.evidenceJa: 何を思えば勝てるのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks what he must imagine in order to win.
findings.explanation: What could I win with turns the question into selecting an external means and weakens the immediate link to imaginative construction.

findings.evidenceJa: 手間を増やさないと
findings.governingReading: Because Strengthening cannot give form to what does not exist, Shirou must add further stages to his usual procedure.
findings.explanation: More effort turns a change in magical process into greater exertion.

findings.evidenceJa: 強化”の手順を教わる前の技法
findings.governingReading: Shirou recalls a technique from before he learned the procedure for Strengthening: the wasteful magical process he devised himself before Kiritsugu taught him.
findings.explanation: The English omits 技法 and collapses the earlier technique into the process alone.

findings.highlight: how was it supposed to take shape
findings.evidenceJa: どうやって、カタチにすればいい
findings.governingReading: Shirou tries to remember how he himself was supposed to give it form.
findings.explanation: Take shape removes Shirou as the agent carrying out the formative procedure.

findings.evidenceJa: 毛足の長い絨毯
findings.governingReading: The carpet has such a deep, long pile that one might sink into it up to the ankles.
findings.explanation: Long carpet describes its overall dimensions instead of the length of its fibers.

findings.evidenceJa: 今も暖房として使われている
findings.governingReading: The stone fireplace is still being used as the room’s heating, rather than serving as decoration.
findings.explanation: Functional says it works but omits its present, active use for heating.

findings.evidenceJa: 意識が消えかける
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s consciousness begins to fade again.
findings.explanation: A mind cannot idiomatically fall unconscious, producing a malformed English description.

findings.highlight: it seems I could at least raise my arm
findings.evidenceJa: さっきみたいに指先すら動かない
findings.governingReading: Although his body is heavy, Shirou is no longer unable to move even a fingertip as he was before; with effort, he may be able to raise one arm.
findings.explanation: The English omits the recovery contrast with his earlier total paralysis.

findings.highlight: I can’t trouble her by letting her know I’ve been kidnapped.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が攫われたなんて、そんな事で負担をかける訳にはいかない
findings.governingReading: Shirou refuses to burden weakened Saber with the fact and consequences of his abduction.
findings.explanation: Letting her know invents disclosure as the source of the burden, rather than the kidnapping and rescue pressure themselves.

findings.highlight: talking to me in that park the other day
findings.evidenceJa: 公園で俺と話していた
findings.governingReading: The familiar Illya is the white girl who spoke with Shirou in the park earlier that same day.
findings.explanation: The other day displaces the encounter into an earlier date and breaks the morning-to-night timeline.

findings.evidenceJa: 覗き込んでくるイリヤを睨む
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese ends Shirou’s reply without narrating a glare; that line is commented out.
findings.explanation: mirror moon restores superseded hostile body language as active narration.

findings.evidenceJa: 不満そうに唇をとがらすイリヤ
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese moves directly from Illya’s speech to Shirou’s uncertainty; her pout is commented out.
findings.explanation: mirror moon restores a deleted reaction and thereby adds an explicit childish beat.

findings.highlight: a castle in a big forest
findings.evidenceJa: 樹海の中の城
findings.governingReading: Illya describes the castle as lying within a dense sea of trees.
findings.explanation: Big forest loses the enclosing, trackless 樹海 image.

findings.highlight: nor will there be any nuisances
findings.evidenceJa: 絶対に邪魔も入らない
findings.governingReading: Illya insists that no one can interfere with what she intends to do.
findings.explanation: Nuisances treats possible rescuers as annoyances and obscures the claim that intervention is impossible.

findings.evidenceJa: 生々しくい
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese itself ends in the malformed 生々しくい; the longer explanation about losing calm thought is a deleted variant and should not be silently reconstructed.
findings.explanation: mirror moon prints two competing completions and restores the deleted calm-thought clause without marking the source defect.

findings.highlight: She says so in a fawning voice.
findings.evidenceJa: 甘えるような声で言う
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese begins with the purity and irreversibility of Illya’s words; the fawning-voice and not-halfhearted narration is commented out.
findings.explanation: mirror moon restores two deleted interpretive lines that prescribe the tone of Illya’s proposal.

findings.evidenceJa: 逆らえば
findings.governingReading: Shirou believes that if he resists or defies Illya, all of her purity may turn into hatred.
findings.explanation: Betray recasts refusal of captivity as a breach of loyalty, morally weighting the choice in Illya’s favor.

findings.highlight: asking me if I want to live or die
findings.evidenceJa: 死ぬか生きるかを問う審問に等しい
findings.governingReading: Illya’s proposal is equivalent to an inquisition deciding whether Shirou lives or dies.
findings.explanation: Asking what he wants removes the judicial coercion and makes the forced life-or-death choice sound voluntary.

findings.evidenceJa: セイバーはいない
findings.governingReading: Illya asserts that Saber is no longer present.
findings.explanation: Already is placed unidiomatically and muddles the state Illya treats as settled.

findings.highlight: I don’t even have the freedom to push her away.
findings.evidenceJa: それをはねのけるだけの自由も
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese moves from Illya pressing against Shirou to his uncertainty about defying her; the explicit freedom line is commented out.
findings.explanation: mirror moon restores a deleted sentence that directly states his inability to push her away.

findings.evidenceJa: クスリと愉快そうに笑って
findings.governingReading: Illya gives a small, amused chuckle as she looks up at the bewildered Shirou.
findings.explanation: Smiles removes both the audible chuckle and her enjoyment of his confusion.

findings.highlight: It’s my decision if you live or not
findings.evidenceJa: 生かすも殺すもわたしの自由
findings.governingReading: Illya says that whether she keeps Shirou alive or kills him is entirely hers to decide.
findings.explanation: If you live or not euphemizes her explicit power to kill him.

findings.evidenceJa: 拒否を許さない妖艶さで
findings.governingReading: Illya delivers the order with a bewitching, sensual allure that permits no refusal.
findings.explanation: The English retains the refusal pressure only as an as-if qualification and omits the disquieting allure attached to her delivery.
